about: A demo run, replayed from a live gpt-6-luna run (1014-130442-c994) at about 15x speed. The plan, every agent's edits and reports, the checker model's one verdict and the owner's two skips are that run's. The evals, tests, checks, merges and budget caps are real and run on a fresh copy of repo/. The model's answers for every prompt the agents tried ship in answers.json, so scoring needs no key. Every complaint is a real one from the CFPB Consumer Complaint Database (public domain).
title: Complaint routing
blurb: An LLM reads real consumer complaints and sends each one to the right team (mortgage, credit card, debt collection and three more). It gets about 80% right; the goal is 85%. Agents try different fixes at the same time. Lucidity tests every fix on complaints the agents never saw and keeps only the best one that clears the bar.
about_repo: bundled LLM complaint router with 288 real CFPB complaints and an eval script
commit_message: complaintkit: naive prompt + keyword parser, CFPB complaints, evals/score.py
goal: Raise held-out accuracy to 0.85 or better without any product's F1 dropping more than 0.05. Tune only on the dev split. Where there are several reasonable ways to improve the prompt, have agents try them in parallel and keep the best.

plan.summary: Improve prompt and answer parsing using dev-only evidence, then validate held-out accuracy ≥0.85 with no product F1 dropping more than 0.05. Parallelize independent prompt experiments and merge the strongest passing approach; preserve the held-out set strictly for evaluation.

nodes.title: Inspect dev errors and establish baseline
nodes.prompt: Run the evaluation on the dev split with misses and inspect the prompt, parser, and score script. Identify high-impact error patterns and record the baseline held-out scores only as a comparison point; do not inspect held-out examples or tune against them. Report whether changing only the prompt, parser, or both is most promising.

done_when.text: Review confirms the agent used only dev examples to identify changes, and documented baseline per-product F1/accuracy from the mandated heldout eval without using heldout examples to tune.

nodes.title: Try explicit-label prompt strategy
nodes.prompt: Independently tune complaintkit/prompt.py using only the dev split. Test an explicit taxonomy/label-choice prompt that maps the six product categories to the requested answer labels and handle common synonyms seen in dev. Do not modify parser or inspect held-out examples. Keep the best prompt version that meets the overall held-out accuracy goal and per-product F1 guardrail, checked only by the required final heldout eval.
strategies: Provide concise definitions and explicit canonical output labels for all six categories, emphasizing answer exactly one label.
Use a compact decision tree and contrast commonly confused categories, while requiring exactly one canonical label.

nodes.title: Try disambiguation-focused prompt strategy
nodes.prompt: Independently tune complaintkit/prompt.py using only the dev split, focusing on distinctions that caused errors (especially debt collection versus credit reporting and banking/payment products). Include clear category boundaries and require a single canonical label. Do not modify parser or inspect held-out examples; evaluate heldout only for the required final gate.
strategies: Clarify ownership based on the core issue and distinguish debt collection from credit report disputes with examples drawn only from dev.
Define category boundaries for credit card, checking/savings, transfer, and mortgage, emphasizing that product mentions alone do not determine label.

nodes.title: Improve robust answer-to-label parsing
nodes.prompt: Inspect complaintkit/labels.py and use dev predictions/errors to improve parsing of model free-text responses, particularly synonyms and answers mentioning multiple products. Keep changes limited to parsing and use dev only for tuning. Do not inspect held-out examples; the heldout eval is only a pass/fail gate.

t1-r1.report: I reviewed the dev misses and prompt, parser, and scoring script, then documented dev error patterns and the held-out aggregate baseline in `DEV_ERROR_REVIEW.md`; both prompt and parser changes appear most promising. The conditions pass: only dev examples informed the error review, and held-out was used only for aggregate baseline scores, not examples or tuning.

t2a-r1.report: I updated `complaintkit/prompt.py` with explicit definitions and canonical labels for all six categories, plus guidance for distinguishing common synonyms and overlapping issues. The held-out conditions pass: accuracy is 0.875, and no product’s F1 dropped more than 0.05 from baseline.

t2b-r1.report: I updated `complaintkit/prompt.py` with an explicit six-category taxonomy, decision guide, and contrastive guidance for commonly confused categories. The tests pass, but the held-out conditions do not: accuracy is 0.8403, and debt_collection F1 is 0.6486 (down from 0.7442).

t2b-r2.report: I revised the prompt with an explicit six-label taxonomy and decision tree, clarifying when to choose debt collection versus credit report and checking versus transfer. The conditions do not pass: held-out accuracy is 0.8264, and debt_collection F1 is 0.6154, down 0.1288 from baseline.

t3a-r1.report: I clarified the boundaries between debt collection and credit reporting, added banking/payment distinctions, and required one label; the tests pass. The held-out gate does not pass: accuracy is 0.8264, and debt_collection F1 dropped from 0.7442 to 0.6316.

t3a-r2.report: I revised the prompt to clarify debt-collection versus credit-report boundaries and distinguish deposit-account issues from credit-card and money-transfer issues. The tests pass, but the held-out conditions do not: accuracy is 0.8472 (below 0.85), and checking-and-savings F1 is 0.8235 (below the 0.825 minimum).

t3b-r1.report: I updated `complaintkit/prompt.py` with clearer boundaries for credit cards, deposit accounts, money transfers, mortgages, debt collection, and credit reporting, and required one canonical label. The conditions do not pass: held-out accuracy is 0.8056, below 0.85, and debt_collection, checking_savings, and money_transfer F1 each dropped by more than 0.05 from the starting scores.

t3b-r2.report: I strengthened the prompt’s boundaries for credit card, checking/savings, money transfer, mortgage, debt collection, and credit reporting. The conditions do not pass: held-out accuracy is 0.8056, and debt collection and checking/savings F1 fell by more than 0.05 from the starting scores.

t4-r1.report: I improved answer parsing with phrase-based product synonyms and first-mentioned-category handling for responses that mention multiple products; dev accuracy rose from 0.7569 to 0.7847. Tests pass, but the held-out conditions do not: accuracy is 0.8333, below 0.85, although no product’s F1 dropped by more than 0.05.

t4-r2.report: I expanded answer parsing for debt-collection and money-transfer synonyms and added handling for answers that explicitly name the primary product, with tests. Tests pass, but the held-out gate does not: accuracy is 0.8403 (below 0.85), although no product’s F1 drops more than 0.05.
